purpose: Teach the infrastructure behind AI applications, including environments, containers, compute, storage, networking, deployment, scaling, observability, cost, resilience, and operations.
staffSummary: Build M43 around one consequential utility situation and one decision: Design the smallest supportable deployment architecture for a bounded utility application and name who operates every layer. The learner must leave with a usable AI deployment and operations architecture record, not a collection of definitions.
openingSituation: A prototype works on one laptop, then fails in production because configuration, secrets, dependencies, traffic, logs, backups, updates, and ownership were never designed.
learnerDecision: Design the smallest supportable deployment architecture for a bounded utility application and name who operates every layer.
analogy: A pump is only one part of a pump station. Power, controls, housing, access, maintenance, alarms, and backup make it an operating system.
learnerOutcomes: Explain The Infrastructure: Containers, Docker, DigitalOcean, Deployment, Scaling Laws in plain English and connect it to a real water, wastewater, stormwater, or One Water decision.
Distinguish development, test, production, container, compute, storage, network, secret, deployment, scaling, observability, and recovery without using one term to hide several different jobs.
Analyze the module situation, identify missing evidence, and name the professional consequence of a weak decision.
Compare how the same question changes across drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, administration, engineering, finance, technology, and public leadership.

Evaluate sources, assumptions, limitations, permissions, and human authority using this boundary: Keep vendor services, prices, limits, and scaling claims dated. Do not publish credentials or facility-sensitive architecture and do not skip security review.
